title: Jacobian criterion for smoothness of a relative global complete intersection at a prime
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $n,c\ge0$ integers and $f_1,\dots,f_c\in R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] such that $S=R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_c)$ is a relative global complete intersection [def-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection]. For a subset $I\subseteq\{1,\dots,n\}$ of cardinality $c$ let $g_I=\det(\partial f_j/\partial x_i)_{j=1,\dots,c,\ i\in I}\in R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ (the determinant [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant] of the $c\times c$ matrix with rows indexed by $j$ and columns by the elements of $I$ in increasing order, $\partial/\partial x_i$ the formal partial derivatives [def-weil-pbc-polynomial-partial-derivative]) and $\bar g_I\in S$ its image. Let $\mathfrak q\subset S$ be a prime ideal. Then $R\to S$ is smooth at $\mathfrak q$ [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal] if and only if there is a subset $I\subseteq\{1,\dots,n\}$ with $|I|=c$ and $\bar g_I\notin\mathfrak q$.

proof.text: Apply Matrix.cauchy_binet directly to B*A=1, with no c<=n hypothesis: one is the sum of products of the column minors of B and row minors of A, indexed by c-element subsets of Fin n. RingHom.map_det and Matrix.det_transpose identify each row minor with the localized image of the displayed polynomial Jacobian minor. If all increasing minors belonged to q, each summand and hence one would belong to the extended ideal q*S_g. IsLocalization.map_algebraMap_ne_top_iff_disjoint makes this impossible: q avoids every power of g by primality and g not in q. This also handles c>n through the empty Cauchy--Binet sum and c=0 through the empty determinant.

proof.text: For an injective selected variable map i, form Mathlib PreSubmersivePresentation.naive for the specified quotient. jacobiMatrix_naive and det_transpose identify its Jacobian with the selected minor g. Compose it with PreSubmersivePresentation.localizationAway for S_g. The composition API adjoins the inverse variable and its relation, retaining the selected map without a separate permutation of variables. comp_jacobian_eq_jacobian_smul_jacobian (proved by the block-triangular determinant identity) and localizationAway_jacobian show that the enlarged Jacobian is the square of the image of g. The image of g is a unit in S_g, so its square is a unit. Thus the composed presentation is SubmersivePresentation and supplies IsStandardSmooth via SubmersivePresentation.isStandardSmooth.

'Only if' (steps 2-4): smooth at q gives g not in q with S_g smooth; lem-weil-pbc-smooth-localization-conormal-split gives a left inverse of the localized d, i.e. a matrix B with B M = 1 over S_g; S_g is nonzero and c <= n (Cauchy-Binet); lem-weil-pbc-matrix-left-inverse-minors (2) (07DQ) with f = 1 gives 1 = sum b_I g_I/1 in S_g, which forces some g_I outside q (replaces Stacks' rank over kappa(q)). 'If' (steps 5-8): S_g = R[x,y]/(f, g_I y - 1) by the existing 08JZ node, the variables renamed so x_I come first and y next; the (c+1)x(c+1) Jacobian is block lower triangular with determinant g_I^2, a unit in S_g, so S_g is standard smooth (00T6) hence smooth (00T7, Mathlib leaf), as the lead's brief suggested; this realizes Stacks' 'by construction quasi-isomorphic to a free module' through the standard smooth node instead of 00S7 directly.
